neighbours.label: the inner word pieces of US place names borrowed from Native American languages (Shen|ando|ah, Win|ne|b|ago, Sus|que|h|anna), as against the inner pieces of equally long European place names
fire: We stopped for lunch in Tuscaloosa before driving on to Birmingham.
The ferry crosses the lake from Sheboygan to the Michigan shore.
Fort Ticonderoga sits on a narrow point between two lakes.
The Cuyahoga River once caught fire near the steel mills of Cleveland.
He spent his childhood summers fishing near Oconomowoc in Wisconsin.
Our cousins live in Kenosha, halfway between Milwaukee and Chicago.
The shipyard at Pascagoula builds destroyers for the navy.
She taught for ten years at a high school in Muskegon on the lake shore.
quiet: We stopped for lunch in Aberystwyth before driving on to Cardiff.
The ferry crosses the river from Bydgoszcz to the eastern bank.
The old castle sits on a narrow point above Kirkcudbright harbour.
The river once flooded the mills near the old town of Jönköping in Sweden.
He spent his childhood summers fishing near Machynlleth in Wales.
Our cousins live in Llanelli, halfway between Swansea and Carmarthen.
The shipyard at Pontypridd once built barges for the canal.
She taught for ten years at a high school in Auchtermuchty near Perth.
